hero.headline: UK household energy bills forecast to rise 26% in January as inflation climbs
hero.body:
Gas and electricity bills in the United Kingdom are forecast to jump by £443 per year starting in January as energy costs continue to push up the country's inflation rate. The annual price cap on gas and electricity is predicted to rise by 26% in the new year, according to researchers at consultancy Cornwall Insight. Energy regulator Ofgem will announce the new cap on November 25.

The sharp increase in energy costs means inflation is at risk of continuing to rise. Official data revealed prices rose 3.6% in the year to October, up from 3.5% in September, mainly because of higher petrol and diesel prices. Inflation is at its highest rate in a year as energy prices have accelerated largely due to the U.S.-Israel war with Iran.

In response to surging prices, the Bank of England raised interest rates for the first time in three years earlier this month in a bid to slow inflation to its target of 2%. Interest rates increased from 3.75% to 4%, and the Bank signaled a further rise could be likely unless the conflict in the Middle East is resolved. Higher interest rates lift the cost of borrowing for some mortgages, loans, and credit cards but can also lead to a better return on savings.

The government is providing some help for households with energy costs. Value-added tax has been cut on electricity bills to zero until next July, and the government will hand £100 to 20 million homes in January. But with annual household energy bills forecast to reach £2,166, Cornwall Insight retail markets principal Craig Lowrey said that ultimately this support can only chip away at the edges of a bill that continues to be pushed up by events in the Middle East.

cards.headline: US forecast to hit $41.1 trillion debt limit by March
cards.teaser: The Bipartisan Policy Center projects the government will reach the borrowing cap in February or March, setting up a fiscal fight in the new Democrat-controlled Congress.
cards.body:
The United States is forecast to reach the $41.1 trillion debt limit in February or March, according to a projection released Wednesday by the Bipartisan Policy Center. The independent think tank predicted the Treasury Department could use cash-conservation tactics for another six to nine months after that, pushing the deadline for preventing a default to sometime between August and December.

Democratic lawmakers have begun discussing raising the debt limit through the party-line reconciliation process, which would avoid bipartisan negotiations with President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers. The projection noted that U.S. debt has risen faster than expected in part because the Trump administration is collecting less revenue from tariffs than anticipated.

cards.headline: Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigns amid scandal, raising concerns about AI investment and US economic impact
cards.body:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned following revelations of extramarital affairs, one allegedly involving a Chinese spy, triggering questions about the chip manufacturer's role in the American economy and the broader artificial intelligence spending boom. The scandal wiped hundreds of billions of dollars off Nvidia's stock market value and created uncertainty around the company's future direction. Nvidia, valued at $3.8 trillion, reported Tuesday that quarterly sales doubled from a year earlier.

Huang led Nvidia's pivot from graphics chips for computer games to chips used in AI systems, where it now dominates the market. He maintained direct oversight of up to 200 people and played a central role in promoting investment across the AI industry. Analysts warn his departure poses a risk that Nvidia could change strategy and reduce spending, potentially triggering a wider slowdown in AI investment with economic consequences for companies relying on Nvidia as a key source of finance.

Nvidia has created what analysts call a spider's web of circular financing, not only selling microchips to customers including Meta, SpaceX and OpenAI but also providing them loans or direct investments. This practice has prompted investor concerns about what would happen if Nvidia reduced spending. Tech executives including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have called for Huang's reinstatement, with Musk claiming critical deals involving Nvidia technology would be lost. A shareholder campaign dubbed Bring Jensen Back has emerged, and Huang said he is open to returning days after resigning.

Investment in AI is expected to exceed $1 trillion in 2026, according to Goldman Sachs. Nvidia interim chief Colette Kress said it was business as usual and the company's growth remains on track. When Nvidia's share price plunged after the revelations, rival semiconductor makers including AMD, Broadcom and Marvell Technology saw their stock jump. Nvidia's board said it is not considering bringing Huang back despite his expressed willingness to return.

cards.headline: Mary Peltola defeats Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, becoming first Alaska Native elected to U.S. Senate
cards.body:
Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alaska since 2008 and the first Alaska Native elected to the U.S. Senate, the Associated Press projects. The victory extends a series of Democratic wins in states President Donald Trump carried in 2024, including Texas, Ohio, Iowa, and South Carolina. Trump won Alaska by 13 points in 2024.

The race drew scrutiny after The New York Times reported allegations that Democratic operatives recruited another candidate named Dan Sullivan to draw votes from the incumbent senator. Peltola's campaign denied involvement. Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered a state investigation into whether laws were broken, and the Justice Department launched a criminal investigation and issued subpoenas to people connected to the alleged effort. No one involved in the race has been charged with a crime.

Another candidate named Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg listed on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., became a factor in the race. The Trump administration sued Alaska on October 22 seeking to delay certification if Senator Sullivan lost and votes for the other Dan Sullivan could have changed the outcome. A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit on November 1, ruling that the administration lacked standing and that its proposed remedy was unworkable. The Justice Department appealed the decision.

Peltola campaigned on affordability, protecting Alaska's fisheries, and putting state interests ahead of party politics. Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and Marine Corps veteran who has represented Alaska in the Senate since 2015, campaigned on his record on energy development and national security. Trump traveled to Alaska in October to rally support for Sullivan. Peltola made history in a 2022 special election as the first Alaska Native elected to Congress and won a full term that year before losing her House seat to Republican Nick Begich in 2024.

cards.headline: Houthi rebels seize control of key Red Sea strait as Yemeni army withdraws to defend Aden
cards.teaser: Iran-backed Houthi rebels have taken full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and nearby offshore islands after forcing the army of Yemen's internationally recognized government to
cards.body:
Iran-backed Houthi rebels have taken full control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait and nearby offshore islands after forcing the army of Yemen's internationally recognized government to

The strait, which accounts for around 12 percent of global trade with 70 to 150 ships passing through daily, connects the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean. The Houthi advance follows the breakdown of a truce with Saudi Arabia in July and a failed government counter-offensive.

cards.headline: ADNOC oil tanker attacked in Strait of Hormuz, one crew member missing
cards.body:
An oil tanker operated by ADNOC Logistics & Services was attacked while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on the evening of November 17, leaving one crew member unaccounted for and eleven others injured, the Abu Dhabi national oil company unit confirmed Wednesday. All other crew members were safely evacuated from the vessel.

The attack marks the second on an ADNOC vessel in recent weeks. On November 10, another ADNOC tanker sustained damage following an attack in UAE territorial waters in the Arabian Gulf. ADNOC Logistics & Services operates more than 340 owned vessels and 600 chartered ships.

Maritime attacks in the region have escalated in recent weeks, with Iran reporting nearly daily incidents of tankers hitting naval mines in corridors Iran has designated as unauthorized in the Strait of Hormuz. The UK Maritime Trade Operations has also received frequent reports of attacks in the area. Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps Navy warned tanker owners that the southern passage through the strait had been mined, stating that cooperation with U.S. military officials would put vessels at risk.

The foreign ministers of Iran and Oman met earlier this week to discuss regional security and the importance of maintaining safe maritime corridors to ensure uninterrupted shipping and trade flows. ADNOC emphasized the importance of protecting seafarers and safeguarding freedom of navigation and maritime security.

cards.headline: Chase, Wells Fargo, Bank of America customers report service outages
cards.teaser: Thousands of customers at major U.S. banks reported trouble accessing services Monday afternoon, with Chase Bank citing a software bug in its hardware systems as a likely cause. Ch
cards.body:
Thousands of customers at major U.S. banks reported trouble accessing services Monday afternoon, with Chase Bank citing a software bug in its hardware systems as a likely cause. Ch

Chase, the largest banking institution in the country, said the issue was temporary and not systemic or cyber-related. The outages also affected Wells Fargo and Bank of America, though Chase said the bug in its systems may have impacted other banks as well.

cards.headline: Spain holds snap election November 29 as conservatives lead polls
cards.teaser: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called the vote eight months early amid corruption scandals and rail disasters that killed 115 people.
cards.body:
Spain holds a snap election November 29, with Alberto Núñez Feijóo's conservative People's Party leading polls after eight years of Socialist rule under Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez. Combined with the far-right Vox party, conservatives could secure a parliamentary majority.

Sánchez called the early vote seeking to focus on housing issues, but his government faced corruption cases involving his inner circle, a migrant crisis, and two deadly rail disasters nine months apart. The most recent crash at Urda on October 28 killed 69 people. Former Transport Minister José Luis Ábalos is serving 24 years for accepting kickbacks, while Sánchez's wife and brother face separate legal proceedings, all of which they deny.

cards.headline: Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and Netherlands to open migrant deportation hub in Rwanda in 2027
cards.teaser: Five European Union countries announced plans to open a migrant deportation center in Rwanda next year, sparking criticism from Spain and human rights organizations over the legali
cards.body:
Five European Union countries announced plans to open a migrant deportation center in Rwanda next year, sparking criticism from Spain and human rights organizations over the legali

Germany, Denmark, Austria, Greece and the Netherlands said the return hub will be ready to accept transfers in 2027 and will apply to migrants staying illegally in their nations who are subject to deportation. The Dutch government said the facility will provide an alternative when deportees cannot be returned to their country of origin.

hero.headline: Central Florida faces flooding threat through Friday as heavy rain continues across multiple counties
hero.body:
Central Florida is under a flood watch through Friday as several more days of heavy rain threaten multiple counties already saturated by recent storms. The watch covers Volusia, Seminole, Orange, Osceola, Flagler, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, St. Lucie, and Martin counties, with the heaviest additional rainfall forecast along coastal areas.

Over the past 24 hours, several communities recorded significant rainfall totals. Port Orange measured 3.32 inches, while Daytona Beach received 2.21 inches and Ponce Inlet recorded 2.18 inches. Cocoa and Viera saw 1.99 inches and 1.95 inches respectively. Wednesday's forecast called for periods of showers and thunderstorms, with heavier rain possible across portions of Volusia, Seminole, Orange, Osceola, and Brevard counties. Repeated rounds of rain increase the risk of localized flooding, particularly in areas that have already received substantial precipitation.

The weather system is expected to bring sustained winds between 15 and 25 miles per hour, with gusts reaching 30 miles per hour. Wednesday through Friday are being designated as severe weather warning days for coastal communities. Drier conditions are forecast to return Saturday, with rain chances dropping to 30 percent, followed by mostly sunny weather Sunday.

The flooding threat comes two weeks after Brevard County experienced more than 20 inches of rain in some areas. Palm Bay is still dealing with cleanup from that earlier storm system.

cards.headline: Forensic expert reviewing autopsy photos says Jeffrey Epstein was strangled, not suicide
cards.teaser: A forensic expert has concluded that Jeffrey Epstein was killed in prison in 2019, contradicting the official ruling that his death was suicide. Professor Michael Freeman told BBC
cards.body:
A forensic expert has concluded that Jeffrey Epstein was killed in prison in 2019, contradicting the official ruling that his death was suicide. Professor Michael Freeman told BBC

Professor Michael Freeman told BBC Newsnight that after reviewing autopsy files and photographs, he believes Epstein was strangled, most likely from behind. Freeman said the evidence includes a deep hemorrhage to Epstein's left shoulder, injuries consistent with being struck in the face, and apparent fingernail marks above the ligature mark on his neck that would be consistent with an attempt to remove a ligature during strangulation.

cards.headline: Massachusetts judge sets March 2027 retrial for woman accused of killing three children after hung jury
cards.teaser: A Massachusetts judge set a March 29, 2027, trial date for Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of murdering her three children, after a jury deadlocked in her first trial in September.
cards.body:
A Massachusetts judge set a March 29, 2027, trial date for Lindsay Clancy, who is accused of murdering her three children, after a jury deadlocked in her first trial in September.

Judge William Sullivan rejected a defense motion last week to dismiss the case on double jeopardy grounds, clearing the way for the retrial. Prosecutors indicated they intend to seek a jury trial, which the defense interpreted as a signal that Clancy, 36, will again face first-degree murder charges, though the district attorney has not formally announced the charges.

cards.teaser: Annual household gas and electricity bills are projected to jump £443 starting in January, researchers say, as inflation reaches its highest rate in a year.
cards.body:
Annual household gas and electricity bills in the UK are forecast to rise by £443, or 26%, starting in January, according to consultancy Cornwall Insight. Energy regulator Ofgem will announce the new price cap on November 25. The projection comes as UK inflation reached 3.6% in October, up from 3.5% in September, driven largely by higher energy and fuel costs.

The bank has signaled further rate hikes may be necessary unless Middle East conflict affecting energy markets is resolved. The government is providing £100 payments to 20 million households in January and has cut electricity VAT to zero through July.

cards.headline: Target earnings beat estimates as shoppers respond to lower prices
cards.teaser: The retailer reported third-quarter earnings per share of $2.65, well above the $2.08 estimate, as comparable sales rose 5.6%.
cards.body:
Target reported third-quarter net sales of $27.1 billion, up 7.1% year over year and above the $26.5 billion estimate. Diluted earnings per share rose 49% to $2.65, beating the $2.08 estimate, with a $0.50 benefit from tariff refunds. Comparable sales increased 5.6% versus the 3.61% estimate, driven by a 5% gain in transactions and strength in discretionary categories such as home goods.

CEO Michael Fiddelke attributed the results to lower prices, particularly in food, and an improved shopping experience. The company raised its full-year sales growth outlook to around 6% from approximately 5% and increased its earnings per share guidance range to $10.65 to $11.40 from $9.90 to $10.90. Target shares are up 63% year to date.

cards.body:
Thousands of customers at major U.S. banks reported trouble accessing services Monday afternoon, with Chase Bank citing a software bug in its hardware systems as a likely cause. Ch

Chase, the largest banking institution in the country, said the issue was temporary and not systemic or cyber-related. The outages also affected Wells Fargo and Bank of America, though Chase said the bug in its systems may have impacted other banks as well.

cards.headline: Major companies directed tariff refund money to executive bonuses, ProPublica investigation finds
cards.teaser: At least nine major companies receiving refunds after the Supreme Court struck down Trump-era tariffs directed portions of that money toward executive bonuses instead of consumer p
cards.body:
At least nine major companies receiving refunds after the Supreme Court struck down Trump-era tariffs directed portions of that money toward executive bonuses instead of consumer p

The investigation analyzed securities filings and earnings calls to identify companies that told consumers they had to raise prices because of tariffs but are now using refund money for leadership compensation. Stanley Black & Decker, which makes vacuums, electric drills, and measuring tapes, is expected to receive at least $298 million in tariff reimbursements and indicated some will go to bonuses.

cards.body:
A software bug in JPMorgan Chase's on-premise hardware systems disrupted banking services nationwide on Monday, affecting both online access and in-branch transactions and causing

The bank said the issue was not cyber-related and that all customers retained access to their accounts and funds, though servicing some customers was taking longer than usual. Chase said it was working to resolve the problem by the end of the day.

hero.headline: Voyager 1 reaches one light-day from Earth, the farthest any human-made object has traveled
hero.body:
NASA's Voyager 1 spacecraft reached a distance of one light-day from Earth early Wednesday, more than 16 billion miles away, marking the farthest any human artifact has ventured from the planet. Launched in 1977 to study Jupiter and Saturn, the probe sailed past the milestone traveling at nearly 38,000 miles per hour. Radio signals from the spacecraft now take 24 hours to reach flight controllers at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, meaning the 13-member team had to wait until Thursday to confirm the achievement.

Voyager 1 and its sister ship Voyager 2, which followed a different path through the outer planets before entering interstellar space in 2018, continue to transmit data about magnetic fields, charged particles, and plasma waves beyond the solar system. Both spacecraft are powered by radioisotope thermoelectric generators using decaying plutonium 238. Voyager 1 now operates on just over 210 watts, down from 470 watts at launch, enough to run only two of its 10 instruments. Voyager 2 has slightly more power at about 230 watts, allowing three instruments to remain active.

Mission manager Kareem Badaruddin, one of three full-time team members maintaining the aging spacecraft, described the mission as one of the greatest human achievements. The team carefully manages remaining power and heat to prevent fuel lines from freezing and to keep the spacecraft antennas pointed toward Earth. With commands taking two full days for a round-trip response, troubleshooting problems has become a slow process.

Engineers hope to keep data flowing for several more years as power steadily declines, though it remains uncertain how long the spacecraft will function. After power is exhausted, both Voyagers will continue drifting through space, expected to remain intact for a billion years or more. Each carries a gold phonograph record encoded with greetings in 55 languages, 115 photographs, natural sounds, and music from multiple cultures as a message for any civilization that might encounter them in the distant future.

cards.headline: Nvidia clarifies that $105 billion loan guarantees activate only after customers secure financing and install equipment
cards.teaser: Interim CEO Colette Kress says backstops like the OpenAI data center guarantee take effect only when projects are funded and operational, not automatically.
cards.body:
Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress clarified that the company's data center loan guarantees, including a $105 billion backstop for OpenAI's Ohio campus, activate only after customers secure their own financing and install Nvidia equipment. If those conditions are not met, the guarantee does not exist, Kress told analysts during the company's quarterly call Tuesday. She described the disclosure as a clarification of existing terms, though the conditions were not previously public.

Kress said Nvidia will continue financing data center projects but will be more selective going forward, prioritizing customers with secured land, power, and infrastructure. The statement follows the departure last week of CEO Jensen Huang, who had aggressively backed AI startups and guaranteed loans in exchange for exclusive equipment commitments.

cards.headline: Historian explores Golden Record hardware as Voyager 1 reaches one light-day milestone
cards.teaser: Glen Swanson's upcoming book examines the physical construction and distribution of the Voyager Golden Record, details largely overlooked in favor of its contents.
cards.body:
Glen Swanson, former chief historian for NASA's Johnson Space Center, is writing a book focusing on the hardware aspects of the Voyager Golden Record rather than its famous contents. Swanson said existing information about the physical record is limited and sometimes contradictory, prompting his research as the 50th anniversaries of both Voyager launches approach.

Swanson and Jon Lomberg, the Golden Record's design director, are co-authoring "Voyager's Golden Record: An Enduring Reflection," scheduled for release by the University of Chicago Press in August 2027. Both Voyager probes continue traveling outward and communicating with Earth.

cards.headline: Suno launches AI video generator that lipsyncs to its AI-generated music
cards.teaser: The music AI platform introduces "Visuals,
cards.body:
Suno introduced Visuals, a feature that generates AI video clips and images synchronized to songs created on its platform. Users can create 15-second videos that automatically lipsync to lyrics, using reference images from Suno presets, uploaded photos, or AI-generated prompts. The feature is available on web, iOS, and Android.

Visuals uses the H3 Move AI model and includes filters designed to block generation of specific artists, public figures, and copyrighted works. The feature requires separate Visuals credits distinct from song generation credits. The launch follows Suno's October addition of a speech generation feature and comes amid lawsuits over its music generator.

cards.headline: Unsiloed AI raises $7.5 million to make business documents usable by AI agents
cards.teaser: The startup uses specialized technology to extract information from complex documents with tables and charts, competing against Microsoft and Amazon offerings.
cards.body:
Unsiloed AI has raised $7.5 million in seed funding led by Felicis to help enterprises make complex documents accessible to AI agents. The San Francisco startup uses what it calls dual-stream vision models to process tables, charts, and complicated layouts that AI systems often struggle to interpret, then converts the information into structured data while showing where it came from in the original document.

Co-founders Aman Mishra and Adnan Abbas, former classmates at the Indian Institute of Technology Kharagpur, are working with customers in finance, legal services, and healthcare. The startup competes against document-processing companies like Reducto and Unstructured, as well as offerings from Microsoft and Amazon. Unsiloed charges one cent per page and plans to use the funding to hire researchers and engineers.

cards.headline: India's Humyn Labs raises $47 million to supply U.S. robotics firms with real-world training data
cards.teaser: The startup collects video of people performing everyday tasks across more than 20 countries to help AI models learn physical operations.
cards.body:
Bengaluru-based Humyn Labs has raised $47 million in Series A financing to supply U.S. robotics and AI companies with real-world data for training models that operate in physical environments. The round includes $26 million in equity led by Accel and $21 million in venture debt. The startup uses proprietary two-camera hardware to record people performing everyday tasks across more than 20 countries in Latin America and Asia, then processes and labels the footage for AI training.

Humyn Labs was founded in February by Manish Agarwal, former CEO of Indian gaming company Nazara Technologies, and Ishank Gupta, a former AB InBev executive. The company says it has 12 paying customers and generated $10 million in revenue between April and October, with about 90 percent coming from the U.S.

cards.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI delivers on unprecedented hype after 13-year wait
cards.teaser: Rockstar's long-awaited sequel combines open-world freedom with immersive detail and a mature crime story centered on two protagonists.
cards.body:
Grand Theft Auto VI, released 13 years after its predecessor sold more than 230 million copies, achieves what reviewers call the new standard for open-world games. The game sets players in Leonida, a fictional Florida, following criminals Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos in a relationship-driven crime story that blends heists, exploration, and detailed world interaction.

The game features intricate multi-step heists, a fully accessible map from the start, and systems allowing players to rob stores, steal cars, or pursue other criminal ventures to fund the protagonists' retirement. Reviewers highlight realistic details including functional public transit, refueling mechanics, and smartphone integration that add texture without becoming tedious, calling it the most mature entry in the series.

hero.headline: England sweep Australia in ODI series behind Duckett century and new-ball bowlers
hero.body:
England defeated Australia by 97 runs in the third one-day international in Hobart on Wednesday, completing a series sweep with a statement performance ahead of next year's World Cup. Ben Duckett scored 133 runs from 115 balls as England posted 328 before being bowled out in the 48th over, then bowlers Sonny Baker and Gus Atkinson dismantled Australia's chase to limit the hosts to 231 in 46.5 overs.

Duckett's century was his first for England on Australian soil after averaging just 18.33 across 12 previous innings in the country. Will Jacks added a 48-ball 59 to support Duckett's effort, compensating for middle-order wickets that fell to Australia's part-time spinners. Joe Root was bowled for 12, captain Harry Brook hit out for 17, and Jordan Cox was stumped as England's innings slowed through the middle overs before Jacks helped secure a competitive total.

England's new-ball pair proved decisive in the chase. Atkinson dismissed Travis Head in the first over for the third consecutive match in the series and also hit Cameron Green with a bouncer that forced the all-rounder to retire hurt. Baker claimed 4-45, including Australia captain Mitchell Marsh caught at second slip in the second over and Josh Inglis soon after. Liam Dawson later took three wickets with his left-arm spin, bowling Cooper Connolly and dismissing Jack Edwards and Matt Renshaw.

The series win represents a significant turnaround for England's 50-over team after they were dismissed for 131 in the opening match. The recovery follows a difficult period that included a failed World Cup title defense in 2023 and poor results at last year's Champions Trophy. England next face South Africa in a three-match ODI series in January, playing in conditions they will encounter during the World Cup.

cards.headline: Premier League panel confirms joint-record six referee errors in one weekend
cards.teaser: The Key Match Incidents Panel found six on-field mistakes in the latest round of matches, matching the highest total recorded in a single weekend.
cards.body:
The Premier League's Key Match Incidents Panel determined there were six on-field referee errors in the most recent round of games, tying the joint-highest total it has recorded in one weekend. The last time six mistakes were logged was early in the 2023-24 season.

The panel's five members review contentious incidents each week and vote on whether referees and video assistant referees made correct decisions. Two errors involved both on-field and VAR mistakes, including a hair-pull penalty not given to Coventry City against Everton and an Arsenal penalty denied despite clear holding before an offside. Four additional errors were on-field mistakes that did not meet the threshold for VAR intervention.

cards.headline: Jai Opetaia withdraws from Deontay Wilder fight on Fury-Joshua undercard
cards.teaser: The unbeaten cruiserweight champion pulled out of his planned heavyweight debut at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11.
cards.body:
Australian cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia has withdrawn from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on December 11. Opetaia, 31, who is unbeaten in 31 professional fights, aggravated a hand injury in training.

Opetaia apologized to Wilder and his team on Instagram, dismissing suggestions he was scared of Wilder's power. The withdrawal leaves a significant gap on the card, with several British heavyweights including Derek Chisora, Richard Riakporhe, Frazer Clarke, and Johnny Fisher expressing interest in replacing him. It remains unclear whether Wilder will still appear on the bill.

cards.headline: Pochettino begins as Manchester United manager after leaving US national team
cards.teaser: The Argentine takes over at Old Trafford on a two-and-a-half-year contract following Tuesday's victory over Haiti in his final match with the United States.
cards.body:
Mauricio Pochettino began his role as Manchester United manager on Wednesday after agreeing to a two-and-a-half-year contract. The 54-year-old Argentine flew directly to Manchester following the United States' 2-0 victory over Haiti on Tuesday, which secured qualification to the Concacaf Nations League semifinals and concluded his tenure with the national team.

Pochettino finished with a 62.16 percent win ratio across 37 matches with the US, leading the team to the 2025 Gold Cup final and the round of 16 at the 2026 World Cup. He said the opportunity to manage United was impossible to refuse despite leaving a position where he had been happy.

cards.headline: Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers accepts record $23.15 million qualifying offer
cards.teaser: Jeffers rejected a multi-year proposal from Minnesota to bet on himself with a one-year deal that narrowly beats J.T. Realmuto's AAV as the highest catcher salary.
cards.body:
Minnesota Twins catcher Ryan Jeffers accepted a one-year, $23.15 million qualifying offer, reversing course after initially indicating he would decline in pursuit of a multi-year contract. Jeffers rejected a multi-year proposal from the Twins, choosing instead to bet on himself with the hefty single-season salary that narrowly surpasses the $23.1 million average annual value of J.T. Realmuto's five-year Philadelphia deal as the highest for a catcher.

The 29-year-old cited ownership's commitment to the 2027 roster as a factor in his decision. Jeffers will return to free agency at age 30 next offseason without draft compensation attached, as players cannot receive the qualifying offer more than once.

cards.headline: Bordeaux draw record sixth-tier crowds as fallen French champions rebuild
cards.teaser: The six-time Ligue 1 winners attracted more than 11,000 fans to their first home game in amateur football after financial collapse.
cards.body:
Girondins de Bordeaux drew a record crowd of more than 11,000 for their opening home match in France's sixth-tier Regional 1, the largest attendance for that level of French football. The six-time national champions, who once competed regularly in European competition, were expelled from professional football this summer over financial troubles that dropped them from Ligue 1 to amateur status since 2022.

New ownership group Park Bench, which acquired the club for one euro while assuming its debts, has committed to a 10-year plan to return Bordeaux to the top flight. The team has won its first five matches this season with a squad built around former Ligue 1 and Ligue 2 players, including Europa League winner Almamy Toure.

cards.headline: Mile world record holder Josh Kerr eyes Los Angeles Olympics and place among all-time greats
cards.teaser: The Scottish runner, who set the mile record in July, discusses his meticulous preparation and ambitions for the 2028 Games.
cards.body:
The Scottish runner, who set the mile record in July, discusses his meticulous preparation and ambitions for the 2028 Games.

Josh Kerr, who set the mile world record in July with a time of 3:42.66 at London's Olympic Stadium before winning Commonwealth gold and the Ultimate Championship, is targeting Los Angeles 2028 as he pursues his goal of being remembered as the best middle-distance athlete of all time. The 29-year-old Scot, who trains in New Mexico under a precisely structured routine including altitude chamber sessions and a 16-person support team, won silver in Paris but views Olympic gold as the final piece needed to complete his medal collection.

hero.headline: Grand Theft Auto 6 earns 99 Metacritic average in critical reviews, tying industry record
hero.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 has received a 99 out of 100 average score on review aggregator Metacritic, tying the record held by The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time since 1998. The open-world action game from Rockstar has drawn sweeping praise from critics ahead of its release, with reviewers calling it a landmark achievement that justifies 13 years of anticipation since the previous installment.

Critics highlighted the game's graphics, storytelling, and world building as groundbreaking. Gaming website IGN called the title unprecedented, unbelievable, and unmissable. Eurogamer awarded five stars and said Rockstar had pushed back the horizon of video games once again, with reviewer Chris Tapsell writing that the game is truly awesome. The Washington Post said the game raises the bar at every level, while Bloomberg reviewer Jason Schreier called it a masterpiece and wrote that he often found himself wondering how it even exists.

Reviewers singled out the relationship between lead characters Jason and Lucia as a standout element. The Guardian's Keza MacDonald wrote that they feel like real people rather than puppets and that she found it impossible not to care for them. Paul Tassi of Forbes said he had never seen a better video game relationship than the one they share. The game's setting, Leonida, inspired by Miami, was described by The Guardian as so lifelike that at times it beggars belief.

Some critics noted that the game's increased realism might alter the chaotic tone of earlier titles. The New York Times reviewer Yussef Cole wrote that the game has matured beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups, with consequences to every action, though he said some of his favorite moments have been careening through streets with squad cars in hot pursuit. Rockstar has not revealed the game's production cost, but some estimates place it above $1 billion.

cards.headline: Glastonbury 2027 announces Harry Styles, Billie Eilish, and Cher as headliners
cards.teaser: Styles will make his festival debut, while Cher performs in the legends slot.
cards.body:
Harry Styles, Billie Eilish, Cher, and Sam Fender will headline Glastonbury 2027, the festival announced. Styles will make his debut appearance at the festival, while Eilish returns for her second time headlining the Pyramid Stage. Cher, who has not toured since 2020, will perform in the traditional legends slot on Sunday night.

The festival runs June 23-27 at Worthy Farm in England, following a customary fallow year. Other performers include Massive Attack, Lily Allen, the XX, Robyn, and Kacey Musgraves. Ticket prices reached £408, breaking the £400 mark for the first time. Additional acts will be announced in the new year.

cards.headline: Noel Clarke trial on six alleged sexual offenses set for November 2027
cards.teaser: The British actor and director appeared at a pre-trial hearing in London, where lawyers agreed on a tentative timeline for his trial.
cards.body:
Noel Clarke is set to face trial in November 2027 on allegations of six sexual offenses following a pre-trial hearing at Southwark Crown Court in London on Wednesday. The charges include two counts of sexual assault, three counts of voyeurism, and one count of exposure, allegedly involving five women between 2007 and 2016. Clarke pleaded not guilty to all charges last month.

Clarke has until March 5 to submit an application to dismiss the charges, with a hearing on any such application scheduled for April. The trial will be heard before a High Court judge. Clarke, known for playing Mickey Smith in "Doctor Who" and for creating the "Kidulthood" film trilogy, remains on bail subject to conditions.

cards.headline: Rob Lowe Says He Lobbied Ben Shapiro for Role in 'Confession' After Major Distributors and Festivals Rejected Film
cards.teaser: The actor called Shapiro after reading the script, which Shapiro wrote and sent hoping Lowe could suggest a leading man willing to work with the conservative writer.
cards.body:
Rob Lowe said he asked to star in Ben Shapiro's feature film "Confession" after reading the script, which is set in Stalinist Russia. Shapiro, who founded The Daily Wire, had sent the script hoping Lowe could recommend a leading man willing to work with the conservative writer. Lowe told Shapiro he wanted the role himself, saying he had worked with left-wing writers and saw no reason not to work with right-wing ones.

Lowe said the film, directed by Václav Marhoul and also starring James Franco and Nick Nolte, was rejected by every film festival and traditional distributor. The Daily Wire ultimately distributed the movie. Lowe acknowledged his representatives questioned the decision but said he is established enough that people know he is not an ideologue.

cards.headline: Berlin-Winning Film Pulled From Marrakech Festival by Algerian Producer Over Morocco-Israel Ties
cards.teaser: The producer withdrew Chronicles From the Siege despite the Palestinian-Syrian director's objections and prior approval of the festival selection.
cards.body:
Chronicles From the Siege, which won best first feature at the Berlin Film Festival, has been withdrawn from the Marrakech Film Festival by its Algerian producer in protest of Morocco's diplomatic ties with Israel. Director Abdallah Al-Khatib, who is Palestinian-Syrian, strongly opposed the decision and wanted the film to screen at the festival, which begins Friday.

Algerian production company Issaad Film Productions, which holds the film's rights, requested the withdrawal despite having approved the selection in June. The festival said it had no choice but to respect the rights holder's decision. Morocco normalized relations with Israel in 2020 through the U.S.-brokered Abraham Accords.

cards.headline: Airbnb where Hayden Panettiere died reopens for bookings
cards.teaser: The South Carolina rental unit where the actress died of an accidental drug overdose in August has resumed taking guests after a brief hiatus.
cards.body:
The Airbnb where actress Hayden Panettiere died in August has reopened for bookings after being unavailable for several weeks. The one-bedroom unit in Greenville, South Carolina, is listed again on the rental platform, with at least one recent guest reporting a stay at the property.

Panettiere, 37, was found unresponsive at the residence on August 16 and was later determined to have died from an accidental drug overdose. Authorities said the cause of death was fentanyl-laced pills. She had checked into the rental with her boyfriend the night before her death.

cards.headline: Hope Ikpoku Jr. lands first lead film role in British horror 'One Night'
cards.teaser: The 'Top Boy' breakout star will appear opposite Ellie Mejia in the urban gothic feature.
cards.body:
Hope Ikpoku Jr., who gained attention in the Netflix series "Top Boy," has been cast in his first lead film role in the British urban gothic horror "One Night." The London actor will star opposite Ellie Mejia in the feature, which has completed production after filming in Norwich and London.

Writer-director Ryan Andrews described "One Night" as a film about addiction, desire, and loneliness set against British nightlife. The film marks Andrews' return to features following his debut "Elfie Hopkins." Plot details remain undisclosed.

hero.headline: Mary Peltola defeats Dan Sullivan in Alaska Senate race, becoming first Alaska Native elected to U.S. Senate
hero.body:
Former Democratic Representative Mary Peltola defeated two-term Republican Senator Dan Sullivan in Alaska's Senate race, becoming the first Democrat elected to the Senate from Alaska since 2008 and the first Alaska Native elected to the U.S. Senate, the Associated Press projects. The victory extends a series of Democratic wins in states President Donald Trump carried in 2024, including Texas, Ohio, Iowa, and South Carolina. Trump won Alaska by 13 points in 2024.

The race drew scrutiny after The New York Times reported allegations that Democratic operatives recruited another candidate named Dan Sullivan to draw votes from the incumbent senator. Peltola's campaign denied involvement. Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy ordered a state investigation into whether laws were broken, and the Justice Department launched a criminal investigation and issued subpoenas to people connected to the alleged effort. No one involved in the race has been charged with a crime.

Another candidate named Dan Sullivan, a retired teacher from Petersburg listed on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., became a factor in the race. The Trump administration sued Alaska on October 22 seeking to delay certification if Senator Sullivan lost and votes for the other Dan Sullivan could have changed the outcome. A federal judge dismissed the lawsuit on November 1, ruling that the administration lacked standing and that its proposed remedy was unworkable. The Justice Department appealed the decision.

Peltola campaigned on affordability, protecting Alaska's fisheries, and putting state interests ahead of party politics. Sullivan, a former Alaska attorney general and Marine Corps veteran who has represented Alaska in the Senate since 2015, campaigned on his record on energy development and national security. Trump traveled to Alaska in October to rally support for Sullivan. Peltola made history in a 2022 special election as the first Alaska Native elected to Congress and won a full term that year before losing her House seat to Republican Nick Begich in 2024.

cards.headline: House Oversight Democrats target Trump family, top aides with document-preservation letters
cards.teaser: Incoming chair Robert Garcia sent letters to 12 figures, including Donald Trump Jr., Eric Trump, Jared Kushner, and Chief of Staff Stephen Miller.
cards.body:
Representative Robert Garcia, the expected incoming chair of the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee, sent document-preservation letters Wednesday to 12 figures in President Donald Trump's orbit, including his sons Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump, Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, former Chief Susie Wiles, and Vice President JD Vance. The letters, which carry no legal force, signal Democratic priorities when the party takes control of the House in January.

Garcia outlined planned investigations into Trump family cryptocurrency business dealings, alleged pay-to-play schemes involving foreign interests, ICE enforcement actions under Miller's direction, and the administration's handling of files related to convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein. The White House has repeatedly denied conflicts of interest involving the president or his family members.

cards.headline: House Democrats open inquiry into Lutnick family Nvidia holdings amid chip smuggling allegations
cards.teaser: Lawmakers question whether Commerce Secretary's financial ties to the chipmaker affected the administration's response to alleged shipments to China.
cards.body:
Lawmakers question whether Commerce Secretary's financial ties to the chipmaker affected the administration's response to alleged shipments to China.

House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Committee Democrats are investigating whether Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick's family holdings in Nvidia influenced the administration's response to alleged chip smuggling to China. Representatives Jamie Raskin, Gregory Meeks, and Sydney Kamlager-Dove sent a letter to Brandon Lutnick, who chairs Cantor Fitzgerald, the investment firm Howard Lutnick transferred to his children at his 2025 confirmation after holding more than $1.3 billion in Nvidia stock.

cards.headline: US forecast to hit $41.1 trillion debt limit by March
cards.teaser: The Bipartisan Policy Center projects the government will reach the borrowing cap in February or March, setting up a fiscal fight in the new Democrat-controlled Congress.
cards.body:
The United States is forecast to reach the $41.1 trillion debt limit in February or March, according to a projection released Wednesday by the Bipartisan Policy Center. The independent think tank predicted the Treasury Department could use cash-conservation tactics for another six to nine months after that, pushing the deadline for preventing a default to sometime between August and December.

Democratic lawmakers have begun discussing raising the debt limit through the party-line reconciliation process, which would avoid bipartisan negotiations with President Donald Trump and Republican lawmakers. The projection noted that U.S. debt has risen faster than expected in part because the Trump administration is collecting less revenue from tariffs than anticipated.

cards.headline: Alaska Native strongholds delivered more than half of Peltola's Senate lead
cards.teaser: Four districts with majority Alaska Native populations supplied about 55% of Mary Peltola's statewide margin, underscoring tribal turnout in her historic win.
cards.body:
Four western and northern Alaska House districts with majority Alaska Native populations delivered a combined margin of about 6,700 votes for Mary Peltola, accounting for roughly 55% of her approximately 12,400-vote statewide first-choice lead over Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan in unofficial returns. The districts represented just 5% of statewide first-choice votes. Peltola, a Yup'ik Democrat, became the nation's first Alaska Native U.S. senator.

In Kwethluk, the Yup'ik village where Peltola grew up, she led Sullivan 136–9. Nonpartisan organizers conducted outreach in Native languages, though definitive statewide turnout comparisons remain pending. Peltola cleared the 50% threshold needed to avoid ranked-choice tabulation.

cards.headline: Generational divide opens in Congressional Black Caucus over committee term limits
cards.teaser: Younger members are challenging the caucus's longstanding defense of seniority as leaders including Bennie Thompson, Bobby Scott and Maxine Waters seek to reclaim gavels.
cards.body:
Younger members are challenging the caucus's longstanding defense of seniority as leaders including Bennie Thompson, Bobby Scott and Maxine Waters seek to reclaim gavels.

Several long-tenured Black committee leaders seeking to reclaim gavels when Democrats retake the House majority in January are facing internal challenges over term limits. Representatives Bennie Thompson of Mississippi, Bobby Scott of Virginia, and Maxine Waters of California have each led their respective committees for at least a decade, but newer Congressional Black Caucus members are openly supporting term-limit proposals that would force leadership changes.

cards.headline: Senators Cantwell and Rounds urge White House action on AI cyber threats to banks and infrastructure
cards.teaser: Two senators called on the administration to coordinate federal agencies against artificial intelligence-enabled attacks.
cards.body:
Senators Maria Cantwell and Mike Rounds sent a letter Tuesday to Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton urging immediate White House action to protect banks, infrastructure, and software from artificial intelligence-enabled cyberattacks. The bipartisan pair asked Clayton, who chairs the recently formed Superintelligence Task Force, to coordinate federal developers and experts to counter the threats.

The senators wrote that AI is rapidly increasing the ability to discover and exploit software weaknesses while defenses lag behind. They called on the White House to direct the National Institute of Standards and Technology to create security standards for defensive AI and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency to accelerate adoption at banks, hospitals, utilities, and government agencies.
